title: Investigation Tagging and Export SOP
body:
Purpose:
This SOP defines a pragmatic, repeatable approach for on-call security engineers to tag, enrich, and export evidence for incidents that touch RBAC v2, audit logging, or SIEM ingestion. The goal is to ensure consistent artifacts for investigations and downstream automation (forensic snapshots, SIEM exports, and legal holds).

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all security on-call shifts and second-line responders handling alerts that involve access-control anomalies, suspicious audit-log patterns, or automated evidence exports to our SIEM pipeline.
- Covers: initial triage tagging, enrichment procedures, automated export triggers, manual evidence harvests, and post-incident artifact closure.
- Not a replacement for the incident commander checklist for major incidents; use in tandem with incident escalation practices.

Key definitions (quick reference):
- Evidence Tag (ET): Short standardized labels attached to incidents/alerts (e.g., et:rbac-exchange, et:audit-suspected-tamper).
- Enrichment Record (ER): Consolidated metadata added to SIEM events (user risk score, role-hierarchy snapshot, active sessions list, token fingerprint).
- Export Bundle (XB): Compressed archive of raw logs, enriched metadata, and chain-of-custody notes produced for legal/forensics or SIEM offline ingestion.

Who to notify (initial):
- Security on-call (primary): #sec-oncall Slack
- SRE on-call for potential service impact: #sre-oncall
- Product owner if customer-facing data involved: reference product rota in PagerDuty

Tagging conventions (must use these verbatim when possible):
- et:rbac-v2 -> incidents where RBAC policy modifications or role assignments are in scope
- et:audit-schema -> suspicious or malformed audit entries that may indicate schema drift or ingestion issues
- et:siem-export -> indicates a manual export is being requested/has run
- et:evidence-highpri -> evidence likely required by legal/forensics (contains PII or exfil risk)
- et:kvcache-hit -> indicates an event correlated with runtime KV cache behavior relevant to request routing

Minimum triage steps (15 minutes target):
1) Record alert id and apply 1–2 evidence tags from above.
2) Capture immediate context: affected user id, roles, IP address, timestamp windows. Add to incident notes and set et:siem-export if raw log export is needed.
3) Check RBAC v2 policy change feed (rbac-v2-audit stream): run quick query: tail 100 entries for user/role in question. If policy change within +/-10 minutes, escalate to policy-owner.
4) Snapshot active sessions for affected principals: call internal API /admin/sessions?user=<id> and save result as evidence file sessions-<id>-<ts>.json.
5) If signs of tamper or missing audit fields, tag et:audit-schema and set severity at least P2.

Enrichment mapping (how we populate ER fields):
- user.risk_score -> combine recent auth failures, anomalous ip, and role_change_count (source: identity service and ML risk engine).
- rbac.snapshot -> export JSON of user->roles and role->perms at incident time (source: rbac-v2 state api).
- audit.ingest_offsets -> raw ingest offsets from Kafka topic for easy fetching (topic, partition, offset range).
- token.fingerprint -> derived from token id hash, included when suspicious token usage detected.

Automated export triggers (systems & criteria):
- Auto-export to SIEM when both: (1) et:evidence-highpri is present AND (2) user.risk_score >= 0.8. Exports are staged to S3://rbsec-exports/auto/YYYYMMDD/<incident-id>.zip and a webhook notifies SIEM ingestion endpoint.
- Manual export route: use /internal/tools/export-evidence (requires sec-team role) -> prompts preflight tag confirmation and retention TTL. Manual exports must be tagged et:siem-export.

Export bundle contents (XB minimal):
- raw-audit-<ts>.ndjson (raw audit entries covering +/- 30 minutes unless scoped)
- rbac-snapshot-<ts>.json (export of RBAC v2 state)
- sessions-<user>-<ts>.json
- enrichment-<incident-id>.json (the ER payload)
- chain-of-custody-<incident-id>.md (who exported what and when, with signed attestations)

SIEM field normalization rules (examples):
- map audit.user_id -> siem.src.user.id
- map audit.action -> siem.event.action (normalize common verbs: ASSIGN_ROLE -> role.assign)
- include rbac.snapshot as siem.context.rbac_state_base64 when size < 4KB; otherwise reference S3 path in siem.context.rbac_snapshot_url.

Common queries (examples for quick use):
- RBAC changes for user: SELECT * FROM rbac-audit WHERE user_id = "<user>" ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50
- Audit ingestion gaps: SELECT count(*) GROUP BY partition WHERE ts BETWEEN <start> AND <end> HAVING max(offset)-min(offset) > 10000
- Session list: call admin-sessions API (internal) or query sessions table with user_id and ts window.

Checklist before closing incident (must complete):
- [ ] Evidence tags applied and documented in incident notes.
- [ ] Export bundle produced (auto/manual) and S3 path recorded.
- [ ] Chain-of-custody file completed and signed by exporter.
- [ ] RBAC snapshot saved and attached.
- [ ] SIEM enrichment payload validated (schema v2) and ingestion status confirmed.
- [ ] Post-incident ownership assigned for postmortem (if P1/P2 or legal hold).

Post-incident follow-up (24–72 hours):
- If RBAC misconfiguration found: create JIRA ticket to remediate policy automation gaps with label sec-rbac-fix and link to rbac-snapshot and offending change.
- If audit schema drift: open engineering bug with audit-team, attach sample malformed entries and the ingestion offsets.
- If evidence export requested by legal: lock XB with retention override and notify compliance.

Postmortem skeleton (fill this after incident):
- Title, severity, timeline (minute-by-minute for first 2 hours), root cause hypothesis, investigation notes, evidence attached (S3 paths), remediation actions, owners, and a short summary for execs.

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Exports containing PII must be marked et:evidence-highpri and encrypted with the legal KMS key before upload.
- RBAC snapshots are sensitive; treat as confidential and avoid including in public bug reports. Use snapshot URLs with short TTL and audit access.
- When in doubt about escalation, err on the side of involving product/security leads early.

Appendix: quick templates
- Incident title template: SEC-<shortdesc>-<YYYYMMDD>-<hhmm> (e.g., SEC-rbac-unauth-20250414-0930)
- JIRA ticket prefix for remediations: SEC-RBAC-<auto-id>
- Example chain-of-custody header: "Exporter: <name>; ExportID: <id>; StartTS: <iso>; Files: [list]; Signed: <name>"

Contact/reference list:
- Security on-call rotation: see PagerDuty schedule (links in Confluence)
- RBAC v2 owner: product-iam@redwood.com
- Audit-ingest owner: infra-logging@redwood.com
- SIEM ingestion endpoint: siem-ingest@redwood.com

This SOP is intentionally pragmatic and portable — light enough for on-call use and detailed enough for automated tooling to consume the tags and export signals. Feedback is welcome; propose edits in this doc or raise PR to the infra automation repository for schema changes.
